summary: Return the maximum product of any three numbers in the array (which may contain negatives).
mainInsight: The best product is either the three largest numbers, or the two smallest (most negative) times the largest, because two negatives multiply to a positive. Compare those two candidates.
canonicalApproach: Single pass tracking 3 largest and 2 smallest

approaches.name: Single pass tracking 3 largest and 2 smallest

personalSolution.notes: Correct and concise. A single pass tracking five values gives O(n).

promptVariants: Which technique solves this problem, and what in the statement or constraints points to it?
Name the technique you would use here and the clue in the problem that tells you.
What approach fits this problem, and which part of the statement gives it away?
cards.answer: Compare the product of the three largest with the product of the two smallest and the largest. Clue: Values can be negative and two negatives multiply to a positive, so the best product is either the three largest values or the two smallest with the largest.
keyPoints: Values can be negative and two negatives multiply to a positive, so the best product is either the three largest values or the two smallest with the largest.
cards.explanation: Only the extremes of the sorted order can give the largest product, so two candidates cover all cases.

rubric.technique: Compare the product of the three largest with the product of the two smallest and the largest
aliases: track three largest and two smallest
rubric.clue: Values can be negative and two negatives multiply to a positive, so the best product is either the three largest values or the two smallest with the largest.

promptVariants: Which two candidate products must be compared?
Why can't you just multiply the three largest?
options: Three largest, and two smallest times the largest
The three smallest numbers multiplied together only
Largest times the two middle values of the sorted array
Sum of the three largest numbers in the array
cards.answer: Three largest, and two smallest times the largest
cards.explanation: Two large negatives multiply to a large positive.

incorrectOptionExplanations.The three smallest numbers multiplied to: Three negatives give a negative product.

promptVariants: Why does sorting reduce the problem to two candidates?
What role do negative numbers play?
cards.answer: After sorting, the three largest are at the end and the most negative values at the start. With negatives, the product of the two smallest (both negative) is positive and may exceed the product of the 2nd and 3rd largest; combining it with the largest number gives the second candidate. No other triple can beat these two.
keyPoints: Largest three vs smallest two + largest
cards.explanation: If all numbers are negative the three largest are the answer.

cards.answer: O(1) extra (in-place sort; Python's sort may use up to O(n)). Track the three largest and two smallest values in one pass for O(n) time.

cards.explanation: Two negatives give +100 and times 5 gives 500, larger than 5 * 2 * (-10). (500: -10 * -10 * 5)
